plan.estimand: Minimum development sample size for survival prediction model meeting Riley criteria on precision
plan.hypothesis: Overfitting-corrected prediction performance (Nagelkerke R-squared) will not degrade by more than 0.05 between apparent and adjusted measures when model is developed and internally validated
assumptions: Riley criteria applied for prediction model sample size with Cox regression survival analysis
Adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.051 provided as summary of expected model discrimination
Event rate applies uniformly; mean follow-up 2.07 years determines expected event count
Shrinkage factor 0.90 reflects anticipated optimism correction
Nagelkerke scale used for R-squared; maximum allowable apparent-adjusted difference 0.05
Precision criterion: average outcome risk margin of error (absolute) 0.05 on probability scale
pmsampsize 1.1.3 default package criteria applied
clarification_questions: Confirm that pmsampsize 1.1.3 survival module implements Riley criteria with the specified R-squared precision constraint and outcome-risk margin target.
Clarify whether 'overall event rate 0.065 per person-year' is applied directly or requires conversion for follow-up duration; confirm expected total event count calculation.
Confirm that shrinkage 0.90 is passed to pmsampsize as expected shrinkage parameter (not as 10% optimism).
Verify that 'average outcome-risk absolute margin of error 0.05' maps to pmsampsize parameter for calibration/prediction precision on the probability scale.
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2022) criteria for prediction model sample size balance discrimination (calibrated R-squared) and calibration (prediction margin) precision.
For survival models, Cox-Snell R-squared reflects discrimination; Nagelkerke is transformed variant used for comparability.
Expected event count = N × event_rate × follow_up_years; this drives both criteria.
Shrinkage anticipates optimism in model fit when developed on single sample; higher shrinkage (0.90) implies lower optimism assumption.
Margin of error for outcome risk (predicted probability) reflects calibration precision requirement.
Output should include achieved margin of error and R-squared precision at returned sample size.
